title: Finite immersion sections for a relatively very ample module over an affine base
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $g:Y\to S$ be a morphism of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and $L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] which is relatively very ample over $S$ [def-trf-relatively-very-ample]. Then there are an integer $n\ge0$ and sections $s_0,\ldots,s_n\in\Gamma(Y,L)$ which generate $L$, meaning that the map $q:g^*\mathcal O_S^{\oplus(n+1)}\to L$ sending the pulled-back standard basis to these sections is surjective [def-pc-module-pullback]. The $S$-morphism $a_s:Y\to\mathbf P^n_S$ classified by this invertible quotient [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry, def-nagata-relative-projective-space] is an immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and its quotient-compatible isomorphism $a_s^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^n_S}(1)\cong L$ uses the canonical degree-one twist [def-pc-projective-space-twist].

source.place: Tag 02NP, lemma-very-ample-finite-type-over-affine, statement and proof. The finite sections are the pullbacks of the homogeneous coordinates under its immersion, using the canonical quotient on projective space.

proof.text: Choose the witness $E$, $\alpha:Y\to P_S(E)$ and $\eta:\alpha^*\mathcal O(1)\cong L$ in relative very ampleness. Put $M=E(S)$ and $B=\operatorname{Sym}_A(M)$ with its symmetric grading. The canonical symmetric graded algebra has this affine model over $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$; the affine restriction isomorphism of relative Proj identifies $P_S(E)$ with $P=\operatorname{Proj}(B)$ over $S$. Retain the normalized tautological quotient $p^*E\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal O_P(1)$ and transport it by $\alpha$ and $\eta$ to a quotient $g^*E\twoheadrightarrow L$. For $m\in M$, denote its image section by $t_m$.

Record the coordinate calculation for this normalization. The degree-one elements $m\in M$ generate the irrelevant ideal of $B$, since each positive homogeneous component is spanned by products of degree-one elements. Thus the opens $D_+(m)$ cover $P$. On $D_+(m)$, the twist has free basis $m/1$, and the quotient sends $v\in M$ to $(v/m)(m/1)$. For homogeneous $b\in B_d$, the section of $\mathcal O_P(d)$ is therefore $(b/m^d)(m/1)^d$. Its nonvanishing locus on this chart is $D(b/m^d)=D_+(b)\cap D_+(m)$: both conditions say that $b$ is outside the homogeneous prime, since $m$ is already outside it. After pullback, the same calculation evaluates $b$ on the sections $t_v$ in $L^{\otimes d}$. In particular its nonvanishing locus is $\alpha^{-1}(D_+(b))$. On that locus the pullback of a degree-zero fraction $c/b^e$ is the ratio of the evaluated numerator to the $e$th power of the evaluated denominator. These are equalities in localizations and the displayed rank-one bases; local ring homomorphisms preserve and reflect units, so the nonvanishing assertion is also valid after pullback.

proof.text: Because $g$ is finite type and $S$ is affine, $Y=g^{-1}(S)$ is quasi-compact. Since $\alpha$ is an immersion, there is an open $W\subseteq P$ containing its image such that $Y\to W$ is a closed immersion. The positive-degree homogeneous standard opens form a basis, so choose a finite family $b_j\in B_{d_j}$, $d_j>0$, with $D_+(b_j)\subseteq W$ whose inverse images $U_j=\alpha^{-1}(D_+(b_j))$ cover $Y$. The affine-cover criterion for closed immersions gives that each $U_j$ is affine and $B_{(b_j),0}\to\Gamma(U_j,\mathcal O_Y)$ is surjective, where $B_{(b_j),0}=\Gamma(D_+(b_j),\mathcal O_P)$ by the standard-open identification. Write $A_j=\Gamma(U_j,\mathcal O_Y)$.

Each affine pair $U_j\to S$ has $A_j$ finitely generated as an $A$-algebra, by the locally finite type affine-pair criterion. Choose algebra generators $x_{jk}\in A_j$. Surjectivity in step 3 lifts each $x_{jk}$ to a fraction $c_{jk}/b_j^{e_{jk}}$ in $B_{(b_j),0}$, where $e_{jk}\ge0$ and $c_{jk}\in B_{e_{jk}d_j}$; these homogeneous representatives are exactly the description of degree-zero localization.

Each $b_j$ and $c_{jk}$ is a finite $A$-linear combination of monomials in elements of $M$, by the description of the symmetric homogeneous components. Collect the finitely many elements of $M$ occurring in these finitely many expressions, and list them as $y_0,\ldots,y_n$, padding with $0$ if necessary to make the list nonempty. Replacing every occurring element by its variable gives homogeneous polynomials $F_j\in A[T_0,\ldots,T_n]_{d_j}$ and $F_{jk}\in A[T_0,\ldots,T_n]_{e_{jk}d_j}$ mapping respectively to $b_j,c_{jk}$ under $T_i\mapsto y_i$. The expressions can be chosen homogeneous because each component is spanned by monomials of exactly that degree.

Set $s_i=t_{y_i}$. At any $z\in Y$, choose $j$ with $z\in U_j$. Step 2 says that the value of $F_j(s_0,\ldots,s_n)$ in the fibre of $L^{\otimes d_j}$ is nonzero. Since $d_j>0$, this is impossible if every $s_i$ has zero value in the fibre of $L$ at $z$. Hence some $s_i$ has nonzero value. In a local rank-one trivialization of $L$ this says that its coefficient is outside the maximal ideal and is a unit. That $s_i$ generates $L_z$. Consequently the map $q:g^*\mathcal O_S^{\oplus(n+1)}\to L$ specified by the $s_i$ is surjective on all stalks, hence is a surjective sheaf map. The same argument proves $Y=\bigcup_i Y_{s_i}$.

Apply the projective-bundle quotient bijection to $q$, with $E_0=\mathcal O_S^{\oplus(n+1)}$. Its free-module identification supplies the $S$-morphism $a_s:Y\to\mathbf P^n_S$ and a quotient-compatible isomorphism $a_s^*\mathcal O(1)\cong L$ for the canonical degree-one twist. Equivalently use the morphism constructed from the generating sections: on $Y_{s_i}$ its coordinate pullback sends $T_l/T_i$ to $s_l/s_i$, and its twist isomorphism sends the pulled-back basis to $s_i$. Thus that morphism has precisely quotient $q$, and uniqueness in the quotient bijection identifies it with $a_s$.

For $V_j=D_+(F_j)\subseteq\mathbf P^n_S$, these coordinate formulas give $a_s^{-1}(V_j)=U_j$ and $a_s^\sharp(F_{jk}/F_j^{e_{jk}})=x_{jk}$. Indeed on $Y_{s_i}$ a homogeneous polynomial $H$ of degree $r$ pulls back, in the basis $s_i^{\otimes r}$, to $H(s_0,\ldots,s_n)/s_i^r$: dehomogenize as $H/T_i^r$ and substitute $T_l/T_i=s_l/s_i$. Apply this to $F_j$ and use step 2 and $F_j(y)=b_j$ to obtain the equality of opens. Apply it to numerator and denominator of $F_{jk}/F_j^{e_{jk}}$; their factors $s_i^{e_{jk}d_j}$ cancel, leaving the evaluated ratio. Since $F_{jk}(y)=c_{jk}$, step 2 identifies it with $\alpha^\sharp(c_{jk}/b_j^{e_{jk}})=x_{jk}$. The $Y_{s_i}$ cover $Y$, so these local equalities give the asserted global equality of opens and section pullbacks.

The affine opens $V_j$ cover the open $V=\bigcup_j V_j$ and the image of $a_s$ lies in $V$ by step 8 and the covering by $U_j$. Factor $a_s$ uniquely through $V$. Each $V_j$ is affine, its inverse image $U_j$ is affine, and its coordinate-ring map is surjective: it is an $A$-algebra map whose image contains every algebra generator $x_{jk}$ by step 8. The affine-cover criterion therefore makes $Y\to V$ a closed immersion. Composing with the open inclusion $V\to\mathbf P^n_S$ is an immersion by the definition. Together with steps 6 and 7, this proves every clause, retaining the same $L$ throughout. If $Y$ is empty, take $n=0$ and its unique zero section: the stalk-surjectivity condition is vacuous and the empty map is a closed immersion into the empty open of $\mathbf P^0_S$; the quotient bijection still provides its compatible twist isomorphism.
